items.question: Who does Tripta Tarunesh work with?
items.answer: School leaders who are serious about strengthening the Foundation Years: school owners, principals, academic leaders, coordinators and teachers. The work is for schools that want systems that genuinely serve children, not just satisfy compliance.

items.question: What kind of support do schools receive?
items.answer: Support includes curriculum design, teacher development, school audits, leadership mentoring, classroom observation, assessment frameworks, documentation practices, inclusion support and school improvement planning aligned with NEP 2020, ECCE policy and NCF-FS.

items.question: What is PlayXploration?
items.answer: PlayXploration is an initiative founded by Tripta that helps schools reimagine play-based learning as one of the deepest ways children build school readiness. It makes visible executive function, emotional regulation, curiosity, confidence, persistence, collaboration, language, problem-solving and meaning-making.

items.question: What is Foundation Years First?
items.answer: Foundation Years First is an initiative by Educational Mentoring India, launched on 3 October 2026. It is a space connecting child development, research, policy, pedagogy, family perspectives and classroom reality, built around the idea of one child, many perspectives, one foundation.

items.question: Do you work with schools outside India?
items.answer: Yes. Tripta has worked in Early Childhood Education for nearly two decades across India and the Gulf, and has designed curricula for 10 national and 2 international organisations.

items.question: Is the work aligned with NEP 2020?
items.answer: Yes. School improvement planning is aligned with NEP 2020, ECCE policy and NCF-FS, and translated into practical classroom systems a teacher can use on a Monday morning.

items.question: Where can I read Tripta's writing?
items.answer: Her newsletter, The Unseen Curriculum, and her articles are on the Blog and Newsletter pages of this website.

items.question: How do I get in touch?
items.answer: Use the contact form on the Contact page and tell us about your school and what you hope to change.
